localTypecheckAndTestReproduction.note: Reproduced main's clean typecheck locally in an isolated worktree (see Environment Note below): npm run typecheck --workspace=apps/web exits 0 once the Prisma client is regenerated against main's own schema. localTypecheckAndTestReproduction.environmentNote: A naive `ln -s pdcswh/node_modules new-worktree/node_modules` silently resolves @sports/* workspace packages back to pdcswh's source (npm workspace symlinks are relative and resolve against their real target's location, not the access path) and reuses a Prisma Client generated against pdcswh's schema. This produced a phantom local typecheck error (PickDeathClock vs AuditDeathClock field mismatch) that does not exist in main's actual source. Fixed by symlinking only third-party packages and creating fresh @sports/* symlinks + a locally-regenerated Prisma Client scoped to the new worktree. Record this as a standing gotcha for any future worktree created this way under this session's disk constraints (761MB free at session start).

oauthProviderUrls.finding: Live Google OAuth signinUrl and callbackUrl are on the APEX host (no www), not the canonical https://www.galaxysportsedge.com host CLAUDE.md mandates for NEXTAUTH_URL. This is the exact 'specific required check' the gse-launch skill calls out: compare the canonical www host against the live auth provider's signin/callback URLs.
oauthProviderUrls.rootCauseAssessment: apps/web/lib/auth.ts:25 sets `trustHost: true` (NextAuth v5), which would normally derive the URL from the incoming request's Host header -- but the request in this test was made directly to www.galaxysportsedge.com and the response still returned apex URLs, meaning something is overriding host-based inference. Most likely explanation: the production NEXTAUTH_URL (or AUTH_URL) environment variable on Vercel is set to the apex form. This is an operator/environment configuration issue, not a code bug -- CLAUDE.md's own environment-variables section already documents the correct value ('Must be the exact live canonical host WITH www').
oauthProviderUrls.riskAssessment: If Google Cloud Console's Authorized redirect URIs list only registers the www callback (per CLAUDE.md's own OPERATOR instructions), real users attempting Google sign-in would receive an OAuth error (redirect_uri_mismatch) rather than a successful sign-in. If the apex IS also registered, sign-in may nominally work but violates the single-canonical-host doctrine and risks cookie-domain/session inconsistencies. Either way this is a genuine, currently-live, unresolved auth-adjacent risk.
